neoConfucianism.definition: Updated Chinese philosophy that rejects Daoism and Buddhism

civilServiceExam.definition: First system of merit based government positions
civilServiceExam.effect: Grew and maintained dynastic imperial bureaucracy

filialPiety.definition: Respect for elders and authority figures
filialPiety.effect: Enforcement of strict social hierarchy in China

champaRice.definition: A quickly growing, drought resistant crop
champaRice.effect: Increased food production, causing Chinese population boom

songDynasty.definition: Chinese dynasty between the Tang and Yuan Dynasties
songDynasty.effect: Era of Chinese innovation: printing, gunpowder, paper money, navy, Champa rice, Neo-Confucianism

khanate.definition: State or society ruled by a khan; organized tribally
khanate.effect: Mongol Empire became the Yuan Dynasty, Ilkhanate, Chagatai Khanate, and Golden Horde

paxMongolica.definition: A period of stability throughout the Mongol Empire
paxMongolica.effect: Enabled safe long distance trade: spread ideas and the Bubonic Plague

sinification.definition: Process by which non-Chinese societies assimilate Chinese culture
sinification.effect: Fusion of cultures; unity across Asia and loss of some Asian cultural diversity

shogunate.definition: A government ruled by a shōgun, but nominally under an emperor
shogunate.effect: United Japan under the feudal system and a militaristic government

shinto.definition: Japanese polytheistic and animistic nature religion
shinto.effect: Legitimized rulers through belief in kami (supernatural entities)

bushido.effect: Encouraged the loyalty and filial piety of samurai; included elements of bureaucratic roles

goryeo.definition: A Korean state that unified and ruled the Korean Peninsula
goryeo.effect: Achieved true national unification of Korea; valued education, culture, and trade

yuanDynasty.definition: Chinese dynasty between the Song and Ming Dynasties
yuanDynasty.effect: Flourishing of culture and trade despite Mongol ruler

mingDynasty.definition: Chinese dynasty between the Yuan and Qing Dynasties
mingDynasty.effect: Last Han ruled Chinese dynasty; expanded trade and ties with the West

minamotoNoYoritomo.definition: The founder and first shogun of the Kamukara Shogunate
minamotoNoYoritomo.effect: Began the feudal age of Japan

genghisKhan.definition: The founder and first khan of the Mongol Empire
genghisKhan.effect: Formed and ruled the largest contiguous empire in history

kublaiKhan.definition: The founder and first emperor of the Yuan Dynasty
kublaiKhan.effect: The first non-Han emperor to rule all of China

marcoPolo.definition: An Italian traveler that gave Europeans a look at the Eastern world
marcoPolo.effect: First European to create a detailed account of his experience in East Asia

ibnBattuta.definition: A Moroccan Islamic traveler who wrote The Rihla
ibnBattuta.effect: The most traveled pre-modern explorer, whose book depicts most of Afro-Eurasia

zhenghe.definition: Chinese mariner, explorer, diplomat, and admiral
zhenghe.effect: Led Chinese naval expeditions to greatly increase China’s overseas influence

transSaharanTrade.definition: Trade across the Sahara Desert between Sub-Saharan and North Africa
transSaharanTrade.effect: Economic expansion of Africa; spread Islam

caravanserai.definition: Roadside inns for travelers along major trade routes
caravanserai.effect: Supported the flow of goods, and ideas along overland trade routes

sufism.definition: Mystic body of religious practice in Islam
sufism.effect: Spread Islam through missionary and educational activities

diaspora.definition: A population scattered and separated from geographic origin
diaspora.effect: Job opportunities, slavery, fleeing from persecution, etc

quran.effect: Guided the Islamic Empire and Muslims' way of life; influences Arab culture

sunniVsShia.effect: Cause of tensions, violence, and wars throughout history

caliphate.definition: Region under the leadership of a caliph (religious/political successor to Muhammad)
caliphate.effect: Formed massive empires that advanced and preserved science, literature, and Islam

sultanate.definition: Region under the rule of a sultan (Muslim sovereign)
sultanate.effect: More structured and smaller designation of Islamic state that replaced caliphates

houseOfWisdom.definition: Major public academy and intellectual center in Baghdad
houseOfWisdom.effect: Helped preserve and build upon European Classical era texts

seljukEmpire.definition: Turkic Muslim dynasty that ruled from the Middle East to Central Asia
seljukEmpire.effect: Islamic sultanates became controlled by Turks; contributed to Turco-Persian culture

mamlukSultanate.definition: Islamic sultanate led by a military caste of former slaves
mamlukSultanate.effect: Halted Mongol expansion; created a period of prosperity in the Middle East

timuridEmpire.definition: Persianate Turco-Mongol empire comprising much of Central Asia
timuridEmpire.effect: Had a small Islamic Renaissance; eventually led to creation of the Mughal Empire

urdu.definition: Indo-Aryan language spoken mostly in South Asia; combined Hindi and Persian
urdu.effect: Spoken throughout India; evidence of cultural blending

angkorWat.effect: Largest religious complex in the world; shows religious change in S.E. Asia

tamerlane.effect: Founded the Timurid Empire (which fragmented after him); fearsome military leader

battleOfBachDang.definition: Last major battle between the Mongols and Dai Viet + Champa
battleOfBachDang.effect: Major Vietnamese victory which ended Yuan southward expansion

delhiSultanate.definition: Islamic late medieval empire stretching across the Indian subcontinent
delhiSultanate.effect: Established Islamic presence in the Indian subcontinent; succeeded by the Mughal Empire

khmerEmpire.definition: A Hindu-Buddhist empire in what is now Cambodia, Laos, and Thailand
khmerEmpire.effect: Source of religious art, culture, and architecture like Angkor Wat

srivijayaEmpire.definition: Buddhist maritime empire based on the island of Sumatra
srivijayaEmpire.effect: Held its power through trade and controlled the Strait of Malacca

majapahitEmpire.definition: Hindu-Buddhist maritime empire based on the island of Java
majapahitEmpire.effect: Resisted Yuan influence, controlled regional trade, and covered most of Southeast Asia

aztecEmpire.definition: An alliance of the Mexico-Tenochtitlan, Tetzcoco, and Tlacopan city-states
aztecEmpire.effect: Waged wars of conquest to gain tributary states; fell to the Spanish

mexica.definition: A Nahuatl-speaking people that ruled the Aztec Empire
mexica.effect: Built a massive empire and Tenochtitlan; conquered by the Spanish

tenochtitlan.definition: The capital of the Aztec Empire, present day Mexico City
tenochtitlan.effect: Most populous city of the Aztec Empire; led the Aztecs politically

chinampas.definition: An agricultural technique using small rectangular areas of land on shallow lake beds

cahokia.definition: The site of the largest and most influential city of Native American Mississippian culture

incaEmpire.definition: The largest empire in pre-European America; heavily centralized
incaEmpire.effect: Empire that developed in isolation, without writing, iron, or money; fell to the Spanish

chasqui.definition: A messenger of the Inca Empire, highly trained and agile
chasqui.effect: Transported messages in the form of quipo, oral information or small packets

quipo.definition: An information recording device consisting of colored threads with knots
quipo.effect: Stored information for Inca Empire, which had no writing system

mita.definition: An Incan system using labor as a tax
mita.effect: Helped the Incan government maintain its power and make public service and military projects

puebloans.definition: Native Americans in present-day Southwestern United States

greatZimbabwe.definition: A medieval city in Zimbabwe surrounded by a large stone wall
greatZimbabwe.effect: Contributed to the development of Sub-Saharan Africa, but declined due to overgrazing

timbuktu.definition: A city in West Africa, was part of the Mali and Songhai empires
timbuktu.effect: Became a center of Islamic scholarship and grew wealthy from its gold-salt trade

ethiopianEmpire.definition: A uniquely Christian empire in Eastern Africa
ethiopianEmpire.effect: Maintained an isolated branch of Christianity despite being surrounded by Islamic empires

swahili.definition: A Bantu language spoken primarily along the East African coast
swahili.effect: Major part of culture and trade along the East African coast

berbers.definition: Grouping of distinct ethnic groups indigenous to North Africa
berbers.effect: Founded and were a part of many African empires

bantuMigrations.definition: Series of migrations of the Bantu people from Central to sub-Saharan Africa
bantuMigrations.effect: Spread of Bantu culture, innovations in metallurgy and agriculture throughout Africa

hausaKingdoms.definition: A collection of states started by the Hausa people
hausaKingdoms.effect: Contained powerful city states that were centers of trade and production

maliEmpire.definition: A West African empire renowned for the wealth of its rulers
maliEmpire.effect: Contained cities that were centers of trade and Islamic scholarship

feudalism.definition: Political system in which land is distributed in exchange for service
feudalism.effect: Localized communities, lowering social mobility and innovation

serfdom.definition: System of peasants being tied directly to the land they work on
serfdom.effect: Low social mobility for the majority; enforced agricultural production

hanseaticLeague.definition: A medieval confederation of merchant guilds in Northern Europe
hanseaticLeague.effect: Expanded and developed trade by reducing tolls and making trade safer

magnaCarta.definition: A charter defining rights for barons and lords in England
magnaCarta.effect: One of the first documents regulating the authority of a ruler

crusades.definition: A series of religious wars facilitated by the Catholic Church
crusades.effect: Increased the power of the Catholic Church; led to contact between Europe and others

blackDeath.definition: The most fatal pandemic ever recorded

littleIceAge.definition: Period of regional cooling in the North Atlantic region
littleIceAge.effect: Long term agricultural crisis and famine, made travel more difficult

byzantineEmpire.definition: The continuation of the Roman Empire's eastern half
byzantineEmpire.effect: Was the most powerful force in the Mediterranean region during its existence

kievanRus.definition: A group of principalities ruled by the Rurik dynasty
kievanRus.effect: Spread Christianity to North Eastern Europe; fell to the Mongols

hundredYearsWar.definition: A series of armed conflicts fought between the kingdoms of England and France
hundredYearsWar.effect: French victory led to the strengthening of the monarchy and the loss of British territory

margeryKempe.definition: A Christian mystic/pilgrim who traveled to holy sites

ibnSina.definition: A philosopher and physician of the Muslim world
ibnSina.effect: The father of early modern medicine

nasirAlDinAlTusi.definition: A Persian polymath who made significant mathematical advancements
nasirAlDinAlTusi.effect: Invented trigonometry, made significant contributions to astronomy

rumi.definition: A Sufi mystic, Islamic scholar, poet, and theologian
rumi.effect: Has had a global literary influence based on his Islamic poetry

ibnKhaldun.definition: An Arab sociologist, philosopher, and historian
ibnKhaldun.effect: The father of historiography, sociology, economics, and demography studies

aishaAlBauniyya.definition: A female Sufi mystic and poet/author
aishaAlBauniyya.effect: She wrote more works in Arabic than any other women in the medieval period

pachacuti.definition: The first emperor of the expanded Incan Empire
pachacuti.effect: Vastly expanded the Chiefdom of Cusco into the huge Incan Empire

montezumaII.definition: The ninth Emperor of the Aztec Empire
montezumaII.effect: Ruled the Aztecs at their peak and during their fall to the Spanish

sundiataKieta.definition: The founder and first Mansa of the Mali Empire

mansaMusa.definition: The ninth Mansa of the Mali Empire and the richest person ever
mansaMusa.effect: Went on a famous Hajj to Mecca that made the Mali Empire famous; promoted Islam

gutenberg.definition: German inventor and craftsman who invented the movable-type printing press
gutenberg.effect: Began an information revolution and mass-spread of literature in Europe

judaism.definition: First abrahamic, monotheistic, and ethnic religion

christianity.definition: Abrahamic monotheistic religion centered on the Bible
christianity.effect: Religion spread worldwide through heavy imperialism

islam.definition: Abrahamic monotheistic religion centered on the Quran
islam.effect: Dominant religion in Africa and the Middle East

hinduism.definition: Indian religion based around dharma (the universal order)
hinduism.effect: Dominant religion in India, dividing people into castes

buddhism.definition: Indian religion based on teachings of the Buddha
buddhism.effect: Religion spread by merchants and travelers along trade networks

silkRoad.definition: Network of Eurasian trade routes connecting the East and West
silkRoad.effect: Facilitated economic, cultural, political, and religious interaction between the East and West

samarkand.definition: City in modern Uzbekistan which prospered from its position on the Silk Road
samarkand.effect: Trading center and center of Islamic religion and culture

kashgar.definition: City in modern west China which grew from trade along the Silk Road
kashgar.effect: Trading center and stopping/starting point for merchants and explorers

bankingHouse.definition: Institutions that handle money storage, lending, conversion, etc.
bankingHouse.effect: Spurred economic growth and safety with bills of exchange and flying cash

battleOfTalas.definition: Military engagement between the Abbasid Caliphate and Tang Dynasty
battleOfTalas.effect: Chinese POWs revealed paper making tech to the Abbasids

sogdian.definition: Ancient East Iranian civilization; cluster of city states around Samarkand
sogdian.effect: Facilitated Silk Road trade between China and Central Asia

blueMightyEternalHeaven.definition: The animist religion of the Mongols, focusing on a relationship between humans and nature
blueMightyEternalHeaven.effect: Religious freedom was promoted within the Mongol Empire

kurultai.definition: Political and military council of Mongol and Turkic chiefs
kurultai.effect: Established political and military unity of Mongol tribes

yamSystem.definition: System of communication and relay stations in Mongol Empire
yamSystem.effect: Increased communication and cooperation across Eurasia

yassa.definition: Oral law code of the Mongol Empire
yassa.effect: Upheld Pax Mongolica; kept citizens in order and encouraged religious freedom

toregeneKhatun.definition: Great Khatun and regent of the Mongol Empire
toregeneKhatun.effect: Notable female ruler; reorganized the Mongol Empire's governing body

indianOceanGyre.definition: A large system of rotating ocean currents driven by winds and monsoons
indianOceanGyre.effect: Its seasonal reversal allows ships to predictably travel

dhow.definition: A lateen rigged ship with one or two masts, used in the Indian Ocean
dhow.effect: Improved water vehicle enabled more trade and assisted the formation of empires

lateen.definition: Triangular sail at a 45° to the mast
lateen.effect: Enabled travel against the wind which significantly increased trade

junk.definition: Type of Chinese sailing ship ranging significantly in size
junk.effect: Enabled Chinese naval dominance and later spread to the Indian Ocean

astrolabe.definition: Astronomical instrument serving as a star chart
astrolabe.effect: Enabled nighttime maritime navigation (no need to use the sun)

rudder.definition: Primary control surface used to steer a vessel
rudder.effect: Made steering much easier; increased maneuverability of ships

camelSaddle.definition: Seat fastened to the back of a camel, typically made of leather
camelSaddle.effect: Enabled the growth of trade based empires in North/West Africa

idjilSebkha.definition: Famous and very productive salt mine region in the Sahara
idjilSebkha.effect: Grew the gold-salt trade in Africa

camelCaravan.definition: Series of camels carrying passengers and goods
camelCaravan.effect: Increased volume and safety of Trans-Saharan trade

djinguereberMosque.definition: Timbuktu's oldest mosque; famous learning center of Mali
djinguereberMosque.effect: Contributed to Mali being a center of Islamic scholarship

transSaharanSlaveTrade.definition: Slave trade across the Sahara; moved 6-10 mil. people
transSaharanSlaveTrade.effect: One of the first major slave networks which lasted many centuries

paperMaking.definition: The process by which paper is made
paperMaking.effect: Mass production of writing material; increased literacy

darAlIslam.definition: House of Islam; refers to countries under Muslim sovereignty
darAlIslam.effect: Its scale and scope created a period of unity and innovation in the Middle East

gunpowder.definition: Explosive substance consisting of saltpeter, sulfur, and charcoal
gunpowder.effect: Revolutionized many facets of warfare; led to the rise of many empires

compass.definition: Instrument containing a magnetized pointer; points at magnetic north
compass.effect: Simplified both maritime and land based navigation; very reliable

paxIslamica.definition: Period of scientific, economic, and cultural flourishing in the Islamic world
paxIslamica.effect: Advanced numerous scientific fields; preserved classical knowledge

spreadOfBuddhism.definition: Spread of the Buddhist religion through its appealment to lower classes
spreadOfBuddhism.effect: Evolution of Buddhism, spread to China and many formarly Hindu empires

citrusFruit.effect: Invasive species showing the scope of trade; changed culinary culture

fallOfConstantinople.definition: Capture of the capital of the Byzantine Empire through gunpowder by the Ottoman Empire
fallOfConstantinople.effect: Further expansion of the Ottoman Empire and a new capital city

safavidDynasty.definition: Iranian dynasty considered one of the gunpowder empires
safavidDynasty.effect: Revival of Iran on the Silk Roads; significant patronage of the arts

battleOfPaniput.definition: Battle fought between invading forces of Babur and Delhi Sultanate
battleOfPaniput.effect: End of Delhi Sultanate; start of Mughal Empire

bakufu.effect: These officials carry out the actual duties of administration

houseOfRomanov.definition: Was the reigning imperial house of Russia
houseOfRomanov.effect: Over 3 centuries of growth and stability in Russia

stPetersburg.definition: Russian port city; imperial capital of House of Romanov

samurai.definition: Japanese military nobility; worked under feudal landlords
samurai.effect: Held political and military power and influenced Japanese culture

devshirme.definition: Ottoman practice of forcibly recruiting Balkan Christian boys to be loyal Islamic soldiers
devshirme.effect: Created a faction of soldiers loyal to the Sultan, counterbalancing the Turkish nobility

janissary.definition: Elite infantry units that formed the Ottoman sultan's troops, equipped with firearms
janissary.effect: One of the first modern standing armies; loyal only to the Sultan

grandVizier.definition: The effective head of government of Islamic states
grandVizier.effect: Consolidated power within centralized bureaucracies at the expense of the Sultan

battleOfChaldiran.definition: The first major military confrontation between the Ottoman and Safavid empires
battleOfChaldiran.effect: Ottoman victory; demonstrative of conflict due to religious difference (Sunni vs. Shi'a)

codeOfTheRayas.definition: Single legal code for the Ottoman empire developed by Suleiman II
codeOfTheRayas.effect: Reformed legislation that would last over 300 years

zamindar.definition: A feudal lord of a feudal estate in the Indian subcontinent
zamindar.effect: Assisted in administration of the Mughal Empire by collecting taxes and ruling the land

divineRight.definition: Asserts a monarch's right to rule is derived from divine authority
divineRight.effect: Contributed to the rise of absolutism in Europe

versailles.definition: A former royal residence, de facto capital of France 1682-1789
versailles.effect: Allowed French kings to consolidate power away from nobles

aztecHumanSacrifice.definition: Human sacrifice in order to appease the gods
aztecHumanSacrifice.effect: Established tributary system to obtain humans for sacrifice; angered tributary states

catholicism.definition: The largest Christian church, viewed as the continuation of Christ's original followers
catholicism.effect: Propogated throughout the world over history
catholicism.continent: europe, asia, north america, south america, africa

orthodoxChurch.definition: The 2nd largest Christian church, prominent througout Eastern Europe and Western Asia
orthodoxChurch.effect: Taken over by the Russian Empire following the fall of the Byzantine Empire

sikhism.definition: An Indian religion and philosophy, the text of which is called the Guru Granth Sahib
sikhism.effect: Gained converts from both Hinduism and Islam; was never adopted by the government

protestantReformation.definition: A movement in Western Christianity that challenged the Catholic Church
protestantReformation.effect: Led to the growth and spread of Protestantism, but also the Catholic Counter-Reformation

ottomanSafavidRelations.definition: Conflicts between the Ottoman and Safavid due to their different sects of Islam

martinLuther.definition: A German priest, theologian, and author, whose beliefs form the basis of Lutheranism
martinLuther.effect: Sparked the Protestant Reformation with his Ninety-five Theses

guruNanak.definition: An Indian spiritual teacher, founder of Sikhism

stBasilsCathedral.definition: A Russian Orthodox church in the center of Moscow, built by Ivan the Terrible
stBasilsCathedral.effect: Demonstrative of the Russian takeover of Orthodoxy after the Byzantime Empire's fall

sacredEdict.definition: A set of maxims by the Kangxi Emperor to instruct average citizens in Confucianism
sacredEdict.effect: Strengthened Emperor's position; promoted Confucian principles

manchu.definition: An ethnic group native to Manchuria who ruled the Later Jin and Qing dynasties
manchu.effect: Struggled to legitimize power since they were an ethnic minority

qingDynasty.definition: A Manchu-led imperial dynasty of China
qingDynasty.effect: Assembled the territorial base for modern China; was the last dynasty

nurhaci.definition: The uniter of the Jurchen (Manchu) tribes, who led attacks on Ming China
nurhaci.effect: Allowed for the Qing Dynasty to take over, established the Eight Banners military system

kangxi.definition: Lognest reigning Chinese emperor; considered greatest Qing Emperor
kangxi.effect: Brought about stability; legitimized Qing power through Imperial art

queue.definition: A traditional Manchu hairstyle, later required to be worn by males in Qing China
queue.effect: Legitimized Qing power; led to wearers being targeted in Australia and the U.S.

eightBanners.definition: Administrative and military divisions into which all Manchu households were placed
eightBanners.effect: Used to unify Manchu people; became the elite army of the Qing

ivanIII.definition: Grew Russia's territory, ending Tatar/Mongol rule and ending feudal fragmentation
ivanIII.effect: Laid the foundations for the centralized Russian state, made Moscow its center

ivanIV.definition: Consolidated power through the Zemsky Sobor and helped transform Russia into an empire
ivanIV.effect: Seized power from the boyar nobility, and established a political police force (oprichniki)

oprichnina.definition: A state policy implemented by Ivan the Terrible which repressed the boyars (nobility)
oprichnina.effect: Organized the oprichniki police, confiscated boyar land, centralized tsarist power

peterTheGreat.definition: First Emperor of Russia, who founded Saint Petersburg
peterTheGreat.effect: Led a cultural revloution that Westernized Russia, example of an absolutist monarch

zemskySobor.definition: A parliament of the Tsardom of Russia's estates of the realm
zemskySobor.effect: Legitimized Tsarist rule, voted the Romanov dynasty into power to end succession crisis

grandEmbassy.definition: A Russian diplomatic mission to Western Europe, led by Peter the Great
grandEmbassy.effect: Intended goal failed, but information was gathered that contributed to Russian Westernization

shahIsmailI.definition: The founder and first shah of Safavid Iran
shahIsmailI.effect: Established a Shi'a Islamic gunpowder empire

shahAbbasI.definition: The 5th Safavid shah; brought slaves into the administration and military
shahAbbasI.effect: Turned the empire into a unified and stable monarchy through a centralized administration

mehmetII.definition: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire who led conquests
mehmetII.effect: Conquered Constantinople and turned it into an imperial capital, Istanbul

millet.definition: Legal framework where the Ottoman Empire granted religious minorities significant autonomy
millet.effect: Allowed effective governing of a diverse population, balancing central and local control

suleimanI.definition: The longest reigning and greatest Ottoman sultan
suleimanI.effect: Brought about judicial and social reform, overseeing the Ottoman Golden Age

taxFarming.definition: Land that was sold to nobles by the government, who would tax the peasants and their crop
taxFarming.effect: Allowed for economic development of the Ottoman Empire; especially benefitted aristocrats

babur.definition: Tamerlane's distant grandson; founded the Mughal Empire following the Battle of Panipat
babur.effect: Established a Sunni Islamic gunpowder empire

akbarTheGreat.definition: Third Mughal emperor; expanded the empire and established a centralized administration
akbarTheGreat.effect: Unified the empire through his religous tolerance, abolishing the tax on non-Muslims

tajMahal.definition: A marble mausoleum commissioned by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan for his wife
tajMahal.effect: Legitimized Mughal power; representative of Indo-Islamic cultural blending

askiaMuhamad.definition: The greatest Songhai ruler, who made the empire the largest in West Africa's history
askiaMuhamad.effect: Policies expanded trade with Europe and Asia; established Islam as central to the empire

tokugamaIeyasu.definition: The first shogun of the Tokugawa shogunate
tokugamaIeyasu.effect: Began the Edo period of Japan, characterized by prolonged peace, stability, and development

songhaiMoroccoConflict.definition: A Moroccan invasian of the Songhai Empire to control trans-Saharan trade
songhaiMoroccoConflict.effect: Moroccan victory due to modern firearms, leading to the Songhai's collapse

absolutism.definition: A form of monarchial power that is entirely unrestrained, legitimized by divine right
absolutism.effect: Led to the formation of centralized states which contributed to culture growth and inequality

councilOfTrent.definition: Council of the Roman Catholic Church prompted by the Reformation
councilOfTrent.effect: Led to Catholic reform and the strengthening of the Counter-Reformation
